raw.query: WITH cells AS (SELECT resolution, variate FROM forecast_metrics GROUP BY resolution, variate), classic AS (SELECT resolution, variate, MIN(wape) AS min_classic FROM forecast_metrics WHERE model IN ('naive','ewma','holt_winters') GROUP BY resolution, variate), fnd AS (SELECT resolution, variate, model, MIN(wape) AS best_wape FROM forecast_metrics WHERE model IN ('timesfm','chronos','toto') GROUP BY resolution, variate, model) SELECT f.resolution, f.variate, f.model, f.best_wape, c.min_classic FROM fnd f JOIN classic c USING (resolution, variate) WHERE f.best_wape >= c.min_classic
raw.observed: 16 of 60 (3 models x 20 cells) comparisons fail; chronos@1min/ctx wape=0.38928 >= best classical 0.38274
raw.claimed: Three pretrained time-series foundation models beat every tested fixed-parameter classical baseline in all twenty (resolution, signal) cells
raw.evidence: forecast_metrics (20 cells = 5 resolutions x 4 variates): best classical baseline (naive/ewma/holt_winters) beats the foundation model in 16 cells, so the universal 'all twenty cells / every baseline' claim is false
